review.notable: MAJOR-1 was a real cross-process lock-steal race (empty-lock window between O_EXCL create and content flush, read as stale by a waiter; reproduced 1-in-12 across 6 processes). Fix: atomic write-to-tmp + fsync + os.link publish, so a lock file becomes visible only together with its full content. Regression-tested with 6 real processes + content-parsing watcher threads.

dossier_06_protocol_mapping.read_only_immutable_copy_on_use: payloads immutable raw bytes; every get()/require() returns fresh copies; mutable-view publish discipline documented for the array layer
dossier_06_protocol_mapping.single_flight: per-key: in-process Condition serialization + cross-process (disk mode) atomic-content lock files, dead-holder recovery, token-matched release
dossier_06_protocol_mapping.bounded_memory_and_disk: memory LRU inert without positive max_memory_bytes; disk quota eviction by touched atime; stale tmp//quarantine debris swept at 6h grace
dossier_06_protocol_mapping.atomic_commit: stage in tmp/ -> fsync payload files -> fsync manifest -> rename dir into store/ -> fsync parent
dossier_06_protocol_mapping.verified_reads: sizes always; checksums per verification policy (default on_read); on_write/always do genuine staged-bytes readback
dossier_06_protocol_mapping.corruption_quarantine: miss + quarantine only while damage is current; require(): absent->KeyError, damaged->CacheCorruption with evidence retained
dossier_06_protocol_mapping.non_executable: raw bytes only at the door (TypeError names pickle); traversal guards on keys and manifest payload names; layout holds only manifests+payloads
dossier_06_protocol_mapping.ejection_vs_inflight: returned hits are fresh bytes; eviction/clear cannot affect an in-flight reader

limitations: Storage primitive only: numerical key closure (profile/plan/dtype/shape/schema fingerprints) is CACHE_GRAPH's duty via put() metadata + digest keys.
singleflight in-process wait is unbounded by design (that IS compute-once for a same-process loser); file-lock wait bounded by wait_timeout_s.
clear() is not coordinated with concurrent writers/flights (documented; loud-failure contract, reviewer probe F3).
Generation numbering restarts if an entry is lost in a crash window (documented; diagnostic, not identity).
